extracted.intended_audience: broadband and mobile service providers; government and tribal entities and third-party data submitters; consumer challengers; FCC filers/registrants
extracted.subtask_description: FCC rules governing the Fabric and creation of broadband coverage maps, the procedures and evidentiary standards for submitting and responding to challenges to availability and coverage map data (consumer, government, and other entities), enforcement and correction obligations, and administrative/registration requirements (FRN).

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge required elements (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A challenge must include the required elements set forth in paragraph (d)(1) of this section, including representations about the challenger's residence/business or authorization to request service at the disputed location and a certification by an individual or authorized officer that they examined the information and that, to the best of their actual knowledge, all statements of fact in the challenge are true and correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The online portal will alert a provider only if a challenge with all required elements is submitted. Government and other multi-location challenges must include all requirements in (d)(1) for each location.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portal alert and provider response timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: The online portal shall alert a provider if there has been a challenge with all required elements submitted against it. For availability and coverage map challenges, within 60 days of receiving an alert a provider shall reply in the portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provider must either accept and correct or deny and provide evidence within the 60-day reply period (see acceptance/correction and denial/rebuttal criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider acceptance and correction timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provider accepts the allegation(s) raised by the challenger, the provider shall submit a correction for the challenged location in the online portal within 30 days of its portal reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance triggers a required correction within 30 days to the provider's Broadband Data Collection information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider denial and good-faith resolution period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provider denies the allegation(s), the provider shall provide evidence (in the portal and to the challenger) that it serves (or could and is willing to serve) the challenged location. The provider and challenger shall then have 60 days after the provider submits its reply to attempt to resolve the challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial requires substantive evidence; parties are given two months to try to resolve before Commission review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to respond consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: A provider's failure to respond to a challenge to its reported coverage data within the applicable timeframes shall result in a finding against the provider, resulting in mandatory corrections to the provider's Broadband Data Collection information to conform to the challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers shall submit any such corrections within 30 days of the missed reply deadline or the Commission will make the corrections and incorporate the change into the coverage maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: "In dispute/pending resolution" designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a challenge containing all the required elements is submitted in the online portal, the location shall be identified on the coverage maps as 'in dispute/pending resolution.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This designation remains until resolution or restoration per the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission review when parties fail to reach consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: If parties are unable to reach consensus within 60 days after submission of the provider's reply, the affected provider shall report the status of efforts to resolve the challenge in the online portal. After that report, the Commission shall have 90 days to review the evidence and make a determination either in favor of the challenger or the provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in favor of challenger, provider must update Broadband Data Collection within 30 days; if in favor of provider, the 'in dispute' designation is removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof — consumer challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: In consumer challenges to availability and coverage map data, a consumer's challenge must make an initial showing, by a preponderance of the evidence, that a provider's data are inaccurate; a provider must then provide evidence showing, by a preponderance of the evidence, that its reported data are accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower standard (preponderance) applies to consumer challengers in the two-step burden framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof — governmental and other entity challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: In challenges to availability and coverage data by governmental (State, local, Tribal), or other entities, the challenger must make a detailed, clear and methodologically sound showing, by clear and convincing evidence, that a provider's data are inaccurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher evidentiary standard (clear and convincing) and emphasis on methodological soundness for government/other entity challengers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fabric dataset requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall create the Fabric, a common dataset of all locations in the United States where fixed broadband internet access service can be installed. The Fabric shall contain geocoded information for each such location; serve as the foundation for all Broadband Data Collection availability data overlays; be compatible with commonly used GIS software; and be updated every 6 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission shall prioritize implementing the Fabric for rural and insular areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation and use of coverage maps
rubrics_metrics.description: After consultation with the Federal Geographic Data Committee, the Commission shall use availability and quality of service data submitted by providers to create: the Broadband Map (areas unserved and extent of availability), a map for fixed broadband availability, and a map for mobile broadband availability. The Commission shall use these maps to determine areas where service is and is not available and when making any funding award for deployment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps must be updated at least biannually using the most recent Broadband Data Collection information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection and use of verified data from governments and third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall collect verified data for use in the coverage maps from State, local, and Tribal entities; third parties (if in the public interest); and other Federal agencies. Government or third-party verified data must follow the same filing process as providers, and on-the-ground test data must use the same metrics and testing parameters required of mobile service providers when responding to a Commission verification request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party/government submissions are treated like provider submissions and are subject to the portal process and technical requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider review and correction of verified data
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers shall review the verified data submitted by governments and third parties in the online portal, work with the submitter to resolve discrepancies, make any corrections they deem necessary, and submit updated data to the Commission within 60 days of notification that such data was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers have a 60-day obligation to reconcile and, if appropriate, correct their data after being notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unlawful submission of materially inaccurate or incomplete data
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall be unlawful for an entity or individual to willfully and knowingly, or recklessly, submit information or data as part of the Broadband Data Collection that is materially inaccurate or incomplete with respect to availability or quality of service; such action may lead to enforcement action and/or penalties under the Communications Act and other laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Materially inaccurate or incomplete" is defined separately; enforcement can follow criminal/administrative paths under applicable law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to file according to rules may trigger enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to make the Broadband Data Collection filing in accordance with the Commission's rules and the instructions to the Broadband Data Collection may lead to enforcement action pursuant to the Communications Act of 1934, as amended, and any other applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict compliance with filing rules and instructions is required or risk enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'materially inaccurate or incomplete'
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of enforcement, 'materially inaccurate or incomplete' means a submission that contains omissions or incomplete or inaccurate information that the Commission finds has a substantial impact on its collection and use of the data collected to comply with 47 U.S.C. 641-646.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materiality focuses on substantial impact to FCC's ability to collect/use data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider obligation to file corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers must file corrected data when they discover inaccuracy, omission, or significant reporting error in the original data that they submitted, whether through self-discovery, the crowdsource process, the challenge process, the Commission verification process, or otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers must file corrections within 30 days of discovery and corrected filings must be accompanied by the same certifications as original filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to update Broadband Data Collection format
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of International Affairs, Space Bureau, Wireless Telecommunications Bureau, Wireline Competition Bureau, and Office of Economics and Analytics may update the specific format of data to be submitted to reflect changes in GIS and other data storage/processing functionalities and may implement technical improvements or clarifications to the filing mechanism and forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FCC bureaus may modify formats/technical requirements over time to reflect technical progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer challenge submission elements (mobile)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumers may submit data to challenge the accuracy of mobile broadband coverage maps. Consumer challengers must provide: name, email address, and mobile phone number of the device on which the speed test was conducted; speed test data using an app designated by OET (including timestamp and source IP address and port as measured by the server); a certification that the challenger is a subscriber or authorized user of the provider; a certification that the speed tests were taken outdoors; and a certification that the handset and app are in ordinary working order and that statements of fact in the submission are true and correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumer challenges must include on-the-ground test data meeting paragraph (c)(1)(i) and (ii) requirements and must use designated speed test apps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of positive and negative speed test components
rubrics_metrics.description: The download and upload components of a speed test will be evaluated separately. A 'positive' component is one that records speeds meeting or exceeding the minimum speeds that the mobile service provider reports as available where the test occurred (e.g., download >=5 Mbps for 4G LTE; upload >=1 Mbps for 4G LTE). A 'negative' component records speeds that fail to meet the provider's reported minimum speeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers report minimum speeds for their service; tests are classified per-component relative to those reported minima.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic resolution and point-hex definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The smallest challengeable hexagonal cell is a hexagon at resolution 8 from the H3 geospatial indexing system. A point-hex is defined as one of the seven hex-9s nested within a hex-8. A point-hex is 'accessible' where at least 50% of its area overlaps with the provider's reported coverage data and the point-hex overlaps with any primary, secondary, or local road in the U.S. Census TIGER/Line Shapefiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: H3 hex-resolution semantics and overlap with Census road layers determine accessibility of point-hexes for threshold calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer challenge cognizability — geographic threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: For a hex-8 to be classified as challenged, when there are at least four accessible point-hexes within the hex-8, each must contain two of the same test components (download or upload), one of which is a negative test. The minimum number of point-hexes with tests must equal the number of accessible point-hexes or four, whichever is lower. If there are no accessible point-hexes within a hex-8, the geographic threshold need not be met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geographic dispersion of negative tests is required to prevent localized anomalies from creating a cognizable challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer challenge cognizability — temporal threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: A hex-8 must include a set of two negative test components of the same type with a time-of-day difference of at least four hours from another set of two negative test components of the same type, regardless of test dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporal dispersion (different times of day separated by >=4 hours) guards against transient short-term issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer challenge cognizability — testing threshold (counts and percentages)
rubrics_metrics.description: Testing threshold: at least five negative speed test components of the same type within a hex-8 when the challenger submitted 20 or fewer components of that type. When challengers submitted more than 20, minimum negative percentages apply: 21-29 tests: >=24% negative; 30-45: >=22%; 46-60: >=20%; 61-70: >=18%; 71-99: >=17%; 100 or more: >=16%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threshold percentages scale downward as sample size grows; once minimum negative percentage or five negatives (for <21) met, plus geographic and temporal thresholds, challenge is cognizable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point-hex dominance adjustment (consumer challenges)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a hex-8 with four or more accessible point-hexes, if one point-hex's components of the same type represent more than 50% of the total in the hex-8 but geographic threshold is still satisfied, the components in that point-hex will count only towards 50% of the threshold. If only three accessible point-hexes, and one point-hex represents more than 75% of total, that point-hex counts only toward 75% of the threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents a single concentrated cluster of tests from disproportionately satisfying testing thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent hex challenge aggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: A larger 'parent' hexagon (at resolutions 7 or 6) shall be considered challenged if at least four of the child hexagons within such a 'parent' hexagon are considered challenged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges can aggregate upward from hex-8 child cells to coarser parent hexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly notifications and status visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile service providers shall be notified of all cognizable challenges to their mobile broadband coverage maps at the end of each month. Challengers shall be notified when a mobile provider responds. Providers and challengers shall be notified monthly of the status of challenged areas and be able to see a map and a notification about whether a challenge was rebutted, successful, or restored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The portal provides monthly transparency on challenge lifecycle and status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider rebuttal obligation and timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: For areas with a cognizable challenge, providers must either submit a rebuttal within a 60-day period of being notified of the challenge or concede and have the challenged area identified as lacking sufficient service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to rebut within 60 days usually results in concession consequences (map correction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider rebuttal data options
rubrics_metrics.description: To dispute a challenge, a mobile service provider must submit on-the-ground test data that meets paragraph (c)(1)(i) and (ii) requirements (in-vehicle tests with antenna inside vehicle when applicable), or infrastructure data that meets paragraph (c)(2)(i) requirements. Providers may also submit other supporting data (network transmitter monitoring, spectrum band-specific maps) concurrently with their primary rebuttal data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers should submit primary rebuttal data timely; OEA may require additional data for adequate review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider rebuttal confirmation criteria (geographic/temporal/testing)
rubrics_metrics.description: To confirm a hex-8 cell, providers must meet criteria for both upload and download: Geographic — two download components (one positive) and two upload components (one positive) recorded within a minimum number of point-hexes equal to number accessible or four, whichever lower (unless no accessible point-hexes). Temporal — include a set of five positive test components of same type with a time-of-day difference of at least four hours from another set of five positive components. Testing — at least 17 positive components of same type within hex-8 when provider submitted 20 or fewer; for >20 tests, minimum positive percentages: 21-34: >=82%; 35-49: >=84%; 50-70: >=86%; 71-99: >=87%; >=100: >=88%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provider confirmation thresholds (notably more stringent than challenger negative thresholds) include geographic dispersion, temporal separation, and high positive-test percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider point-hex dominance adjustment (rebuttal)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a hex-8 with four or more accessible point-hexes, if one point-hex's test components of same type represent more than 50% of the total but geographic threshold still satisfied, components in that point-hex will count only toward 50% of the threshold. If only three accessible point-hexes and one point-hex represents >75%, that point-hex counts only toward 75% of the threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors the challenger-side adjustment to avoid single-point skewing of provider confirmations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of approved speed-test apps and methodology reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a mobile device running either a Commission-developed app (e.g., the FCC Speed Test app), another speed test app approved by OET, or other software provided that the software adopts the test methodology and collects the required metrics. Providers must submit a complete description of methodologies used to collect their data and must substantiate their data through certification of a qualified engineer or official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any alternative app/software must replicate approved methodology and collect required metrics; providers must document methodology and provide engineer certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Device requirements for provider testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of an appropriate device: using a device that is able to interface with drive test software and/or runs on the Android operating system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers must use test equipment compatible with drive-test tools or Android-based devices as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infrastructure-only rebuttal limited scope and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A mobile service provider that chooses to rebut with infrastructure data may do so only to identify invalid or non-representative speed tests within the challenger data. The provider must submit the same data required for Commission verification requests, including information on cell sites and antennas used to provide service in the challenged area. A provider may submit only infrastructure data to rebut a challenge if specific extenuating circumstances apply (e.g., maintenance/temporary outage with documentation; challenger device incompatible with provider-modeled bands; tests taken during a special event; abnormal cell loading with cell-loading data; challenger devices using data plans that cause throttling; or tests conducted while roaming or by MVNO customers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infrastructure rebuttals are narrowly allowed and require site/sector footprints, outage details, band-specific footprints, cell-loading evidence, or device identification depending on the claimed extenuating circumstance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation and recalculation of challenged hexagons
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission determines, based on infrastructure data submitted by providers, that challenger speed tests are invalid, such challenge speed tests shall be ruled void, and the Commission shall recalculate the challenged hexagons after removing any invalidated challenger speed tests and consider any challenged hexagons that no longer meet the challenge creation threshold to be restored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission recalculation may restore prior status if removal of invalid tests reduces challenge below thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge resolution timeline (staff)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission staff will resolve the challenge within 90 days following the 60th day after which the provider is notified of the challenge (i.e., after the rebuttal deadline), except where OEA requests supplemental information — in which case the 90-day clock begins after the deadline for supplemental data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The typical adjudication timeline is 60 days (provider reply) + up to 90 days of staff review thereafter (subject to extensions for supplemental data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-resolution provider remedial reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: If a mobile service provider that failed to rebut a challenge subsequently takes remedial action to improve coverage at the challenged location, the provider must notify the Commission of actions taken and provide either on-the-ground test data or infrastructure data to verify improved coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providers that act to remediate must provide verification data to demonstrate improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-determination consequences — successful rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: When a mobile service provider successfully rebuts a challenge, the area confirmed to have coverage shall be ineligible for challenge until the next biannual broadband availability data filing (six months after the later of either the end of the 60-day response period or the resolution of the challenge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful rebuttal grants a temporary shield (approximately six months) from re-challenge for that area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-determination consequences — restored hexagon and re-challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: A challenged area may be restored to an unchallenged state if provider data mean there is no longer sufficient evidence to sustain the challenge but the provider's data fall short of confirming the area. A restored hexagon would be subject to challenge at any time in the future as challengers submit new speed test data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration is distinct from confirmed coverage; restored areas remain open to future challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-determination consequences — provider loses or concedes challenge (correction layer)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a provider concedes or loses a challenge, the provider must file, within 30 days, geospatial data depicting the challenged area shown to lack sufficient service. This data will constitute a correction layer to the provider's original propagation model-based coverage map and Commission staff will use it to update the broadband coverage map. If provider does not later improve coverage, it must include this correction layer in subsequent filings to indicate areas shown to lack service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction layers are mandatory within 30 days after losing/conceding and must be carried forward until coverage improved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission consideration of other data sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Commission staff are permitted to consider other relevant data to support a provider's rebuttal (including on-the-ground or infrastructure data not submitted as the primary rebuttal). If OEA concludes any such data sources are sufficiently reliable, it will specify standards/specifications and issue public notice adding the data source to alternatives available to providers to rebut a consumer challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OEA may expand accepted data sources through specification and public notice if reliability standards are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cognizable challenge thresholds apply equally to government/other-entity challengers
rubrics_metrics.description: State, local, and Tribal governmental entities and other entities or individuals may submit challenges and must provide data meeting the same metrics and testing parameters as mobile providers when verifying coverage (government challengers may provide IMEI instead of timestamp). Their submissions must include methodology description and certification by qualified engineer/official, and tests must be taken outdoors using a provider-advertised compatible device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government and other entity challengers are held to the same H3/threshold criteria as consumer challenges (paragraph (e)(2)), but have additional certification and methodology requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider notification and correction responsibilities for third-party/government submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers shall review verified data submitted by governments/third parties, work to resolve discrepancies, make necessary corrections, and submit updated data within 60 days of notification of such submissions in the online portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reiterates provider duty to engage with third-party submissions and correct within 60 days when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: FCC Registration Number (FRN) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The FRN is a 10-digit unique identifying number assigned to entities doing business with the Commission. It must be obtained by anyone doing business with the Commission (including, but not limited to, those required to pay statutory charges, applying for a license, participating in auctions, holding auction licenses, paying statutory charges on behalf of others, or participating in the Schools and Libraries Universal Service Support Program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRN is obtained via CORES online or by filing Form 160; it is required for many filings and payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information required to obtain/register an FRN and update timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: When registering for an FRN through CORES, an entity's name, entity type, contact name and title, address, valid email address, and taxpayer identifying number (TIN) must be provided. Registrants shall update this information within 10 business days of any change (online or via FCC Form 161).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely updates (10 business days) are mandatory to keep FRN contact and tax info current.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple FRNs and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A business may obtain as many FRNs as it deems appropriate; each subsidiary with a different TIN must obtain a separate FRN. Multiple FRNs shall not be obtained to evade payment of fees or other regulatory responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FRN assignment should reflect legitimate organizational and TIN distinctions; misuse to evade obligations is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision and use of FRN in Commission filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The FRN must be provided with any filings requiring payment of statutory charges, anyone applying for a license, participating in auctions, making up-front payments or deposits, making payments on auction loans, contributing to the Universal Service Fund, participating in the Schools and Libraries program, paying forfeitures or other payments. Electronic filing systems for filings that require the FRN will not accept a filing without the appropriate FRN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a filer lacks an FRN, the system will direct them to CORES; filings submitted without FRN will be returned or dismissed except in limited circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty and cure procedures for missing/invalid FRN
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic filing systems will not accept filings that require an FRN without it; filings submitted without an FRN will be returned or dismissed except as provided elsewhere. Where the Commission has not established a filing deadline for an application, a missing or invalid FRN on such an application may be corrected and the application resubmitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filers should obtain valid FRN before attempting filings that require it; if no deadline, some corrections are permitted and resubmission allowed.
